26:23: (110) All mavo'ot, etc. — whether closed on one side, whether open on both sides, whether wide up to ten amot, whether more than ten amot:
26:24: (111) For all our mavo'ot, etc. — this is because in our mavo'ot there are no houses and courtyards open into them, and therefore they are not permitted by lechi and korah as the mavo permission law; and although in a courtyard two lechayim on two sides suffice without tzurat hapetach, nevertheless because sometimes the mavo is open on both sides, then certainly one must be stringent that it requires tzurat hapetach even without houses and courtyards open into it, because its head is open to reshus ha-rabbim or karmelit, or because sometimes it is wider than ten, for in this even in a courtyard tzurat hapetach is required by law, as in seif 2; therefore the practice was always to make tzurat hapetach. And behold, on the other side of a mavo, if the width is not more than ten amot, there are views among Acharonim — the view of many of them is that there in any case two lechayim on two sides suffice and tzurat hapetach is not required; their reason is that either way, if its law is like an open mavo, we also hold below in siman 364 that tzurat hapetach is not required except on one side, and on the other side one lechi or korah suffices; and if its law is like a courtyard, as explained, behold in any case two lechayim suffice; and some Acharonim side that from the practice one should make tzurat hapetach on every side. And certainly l'chatchila one must be careful in this; but in a place of need, such as if the rope over the lechayim broke on Shabbat or any similar case, it appears one may rely on them to be lenient where the width is not more than ten amot, even if it is fully breached. And behold, in our mavo'ot mentioned above that have no houses and courtyards open into them, if it is a crooked mavo, there are views among Acharonim whether correction is required in its bend as explained below in siman 364 seif 3; some say that since from the outset its law is like a courtyard, no correction is needed there, and what they do at its two heads suffices; and some are stringent in this, and the practice is to be lenient. And know further that what is explained that in our towns tzurat hapetach is required — this is in towns not surrounded by a wall, or surrounded by a wall and the wall was breached to reshus ha-rabbim or karmelit more than ten amot; but when surrounded by a wall and the wall was not breached, only that one must correct and divide between where Jews live and where gentiles live so they should not forbid Jews to carry — there one need not make tzurat hapetach, but a pas four tefachim wide or two pasin of mashehuyin suffices when breached there fully and the place is not wider than ten amot where one wishes to make the correction (even if the mavo in the middle is wider than ten amot), for this city has complete courtyard law. And when no correction was made between Jew and gentile, the law here is also like a courtyard, that it is permitted to carry vessels that rested within it, but not to a house and not from house to courtyard:
26:25: (112) Beneath the rope, etc. — and since the reeds below are ten tefachim high, no further reeds are needed above to tie the rope on them; rather he can tie the rope opposite them even on a roof above this and that, as we hold above at the end of siman 362 that the upper reed need not touch the lower reeds. Also that which is explained above at the end of siman 362, that one should not tie the upper reed or rope from the side of the reeds but only above upon them — here, when tying the rope above on the roof on some reed, it is not relevant to be precise about the manner of tying whether on top or from the side, provided the lower reeds are aligned beneath the rope. If there is a roof interrupting between the height of the rope and the lower reeds, it is not tzurat hapetach in this, since the roof interrupts between the rope and the reeds; and one does not make tzurat hapetach in such a matter, but must open a large hole in the roof above opposite the reeds so the reeds are aligned beneath the rope without interruption:
26:26: (113) Two reeds — on the ground, but the mavo walls are not counted in place of the reeds. And if there is a protruding pillar in the wall, it is judged as a reed if they relied on it from erev Shabbat, for it is no worse than lechi in seif 11. And the same when projections come out from the wall, less and less than three tefachim up to less than three tefachim near the ground — one may rely on them from erev Shabbat for reeds of tzurat hapetach, provided they are exposed above beneath the rope; and some are stringent with such projections that are not made in the manner of doorposts of an opening, and it is not considered an opening. If one places the reeds inside the house or inside the fence surrounding it on four sides, it is nothing; and even if he placed one reed there, it also does not help:
26:27: (114) Aligned beneath the rope — and if something protrudes from the side, it is invalid:
26:28: (115) In the category of tzurat hapetach — meaning, and it helps even when more than ten amot:
27:_: (116) Whose length is more than its width — even any amount [Gemara]; and its length is called the way of entry. And it is not judged as a courtyard unless its length and width are equal, or its width exceeds its length [Magen Avraham]:
28:_: (117) That does not have three tefachim in its width — and commentators wrote that if its opening does not have width of three, no correction is required even if inside it is very wide; and likewise for the view that holds we require specifically width of four — it deals when there was width of four in all the walls, but where it narrows near its opening, no correction is required even if inside is very wide. And behold from the Mechaber it appears he holds primarily like the first view, that where it is three wide correction is required; and see Darkhei Moshe who disagrees, and his view is that we can be lenient like the other view, see there; and in my humble opinion it appears that even if we are stringent like the first view, that where it is three wide correction is required — this is specifically where inside it was at least four wide but narrows at its opening as explained; but where throughout it is not four wide, certainly there is room to be lenient:
29:א: (118) Ends at the sea — meaning that the mavo had two sides from houses and courtyards, and its two heads east and west — one ended at the sea and one ended at a public garbage heap ten tefachim high from the ground; therefore it needs nothing, for the sea is also considered a partition ten tefachim deep at its edge, and water does not nullify the partition, as written siman 356; and Magen Avraham wrote that here it deals with a place where ships do not pass there to the port, for otherwise many come and nullify the partition; but several Acharonim disagree on this and hold that even when ships pass there, the partition at the sea edge is not nullified thereby. [However, when one head of the mavo ends at a river and there is a bridge over it where many walk to the other side, it appears from several Acharonim that through the bridge the partition is nullified and tzurat hapetach must be made at the place of the bridge.] And all this is specifically when the sea or river edge was ten tefachim deep; but if the sea and river edge slopes and continues, if along the slope four amot it is still not ten tefachim high, it is not a partition, for it is like level ground. And all this when the river is immediately adjacent to the head of the mavo; but if it is distant from the houses more than ten amot, correction is required, for that place is breached; and if it freezes in winter months, then the partition is nullified and it is forbidden to carry; and some Acharonim hold the partition is not nullified by freezing. And if the river edge is high and ten tefachim collect within four amot up to the place of freezing, certainly there is room to be lenient:
29:ב: (119) Is not made to be cleared — for all day they throw their refuse and manure there and its height will not diminish; but an individual's garbage heap, although now it is ten tefachim high, tomorrow it will be cleaned and its height will be lacking; and if we permit now to carry, they will also carry later when its height is lacking:
29:ג: (120) And we are not concerned, etc. — meaning also we are not concerned lest the partition on the sea side be ruined and it be found that the mavo has no fourth partition:
29:ד: (121) The sea rises as a sandbar — for such is the way of the sea, that it raises sand and stones at its edge and shortens and becomes land the width of a parasang, and the partitions are nullified and they also carry in mavo'ot as at first [and all this when there is no slope except at the place of the water alone; but if on its edge there is a slope that collects ten tefachim within four amot, this is considered a partition in every regard]; and Acharonim agreed to be stringent like this view, and specifically for seas; but for rivers we are not concerned that a sandbar will rise, and we consider the river edge a partition when it has ten tefachim height [however rivers whose way is to dry in summer, and when they dry their slope does not have ten tefachim high within four amot — one should forbid without correction even when not yet dry, for we are concerned it will dry without awareness]. And in any case we require that the river be immediately adjacent to the head of the mavo; but if it is distant from the houses more than ten amot, correction is required, for that place is breached; and if rivers freeze in winter months, then the partition is nullified and it is forbidden to carry; and some Acharonim hold the partition is not nullified by freezing. And if the river edge is high and ten tefachim collect within four amot up to the place of freezing, certainly there is room to be lenient:
29:ה: (122) And there is no partition here — and therefore correction is required like any mavo breached on the fourth side, by tzurat hapetach or lechi or korah. A city surrounded by a ditch ten tefachim deep and four tefachim wide is as surrounded by a wall, and no correction is required; and if there is a bridge over the ditch where they walk to the city's mavo'ot, it was explained above that correction must be made there:
30:א: (123) That one side is long — and its wall extends to reshus ha-rabbim more than the other wall:
30:ב: (124) Even if the side, etc. — four amot — and the same even if less than this, he places only opposite the short side specifically and not diagonally; and the reason is that korah is made for recognition so they should not come to confuse with reshus ha-rabbim; and diagonally there is no recognition — meaning, if he places it diagonally and uses on the long side opposite the long, where there is no side opposite it, the viewer will say it is permitted to use reshus ha-rabbim, because that excess does not appear to be from the mavo; and this is the reason he later permitted in Shulchan Aruch to place the korah inside the mavo diagonally, for there they will not come through this to err and permit use in reshus ha-rabbim:
30:ג: (125) He should make tzurat hapetach there diagonally — and use on the short opposite the short and on the long opposite the long; and the reason is that tzurat hapetach is like a complete partition, and a complete partition certainly helps even diagonally, and even if the mavo opening width were more than ten amot, it is also permitted through tzurat hapetach, as at the beginning of siman 366; but if he places one lechi at the long side and one lechi at the short side, they do not help to use diagonally, and even if the diagonal were not more than ten amot, for although lechi is not only because of recognition but because of partition, nevertheless a lechi on the long side does not help to permit use next to it, since there is no partition opposite it, and it is not permitted to use except opposite the lechi standing on the short side, which permits only directly opposite it. However, this is specifically in a mavo permitted by one lechi; but in a courtyard requiring two pasin, or in our mavo'ot that have courtyard law, even up to the short place one is also not permitted to use, since we cannot join to it the other lechi that does not stand opposite it; therefore one must be careful where placing two lechayim to place them level opposite one another and not diagonally [Chayei Adam]; and tzurat hapetach helps even diagonally, as explained. Rashba's novellae wrote that tzurat hapetach helps even if one side exceeds its fellow by four amot and more, for it is like a complete partition:
30:ד: (126) He may place, etc. — see Taz who sides that specifically if diagonally it is not more than ten amot, for otherwise it is forbidden; and see Biur Halacha:
31:א: (127) Until they join together — meaning that they participate together; and the reason is that behold the way of mavo'ot is that after correcting them with lechi or korah, all residents of the mavo participate together [for when they do not participate they will be forbidden to take out from the courtyards to the mavo]; and since the custom is thus, the mavo residents are again forbidden to divide into halves and each make participation by himself, for these forbid those, because it is like a mavo where one of the courtyards forgot and did not participate, which forbids the whole:
31:ב: (128) And they did not make, etc. — for since they did not make a lechi and cannot carry in the mavo, they are not fit to participate together; therefore they cannot forbid the inner one, even if they have habitual passage upon it [Peri Megadim]:
31:ג: (129) From it outward — forbidden — for we consider as if the mavo began from the lechi inward:
31:ד: (130) But if they made in the middle, etc. — in this the domains are divided from one another, and it is as if there is a partition between them, and they cannot forbid one another; and specifically when they do not have habitual passage one upon the other, such as if they have another opening; but otherwise even a door does not help:
31:ה: (131) Two pasin — of mashehuyin, something from here and something from here; and even a courtyard can be divided in such a manner. A city surrounded by a wall and the gates are locked at night and one gate is not locked — nevertheless through that gate it is like lechi; through that opening one may not divide it in halves; but if a breach was made, its qualification was nullified [and see siman 365 seif 2 through which breach the qualification was nullified] of the city, and they can join half and leave half:
